Hi Clara,

Thanks — we have filled out the questionnaire and attached supporting artifacts. Highlights for quick review:
- Deployment: Redwood supports hosted (SaaS), Dedicated (customer-reserved GPU pools), and Private (VPC/on-prem) modes. We list recommended options per BigCorp's data residency and latency needs in section B.
- Metering: Usage-based billing (per-token for generation, per-embedding for vector operations). We provide metering records via our billing API and can emit marketplace-compatible usage reports on a daily cadence.
- Security: SOC2 Type II (summary attached), TLS in transit, customer-managed KMS integrations for Private deployments.
- SLAs: Standard enterprise SLA (99.9% uptime for Dedicated), 24/7 pager-backed escalations for Sev1.

Attachments: BigCorp_Cloud_Marketplace_Questionnaire_v1.xlsx (completed), redwood_network_diagram_2027-03.pdf, SOC2-Summary-Excerpt.pdf, redwood_marketplace_terms_SOW-draft.docx

If helpful, we can walk through items 8–12 (network/firewall requirements) with your infra team on Thursday 3/25 (9–11am PT).

Best,

Thanks for the questionnaire. A few follow-ups from the tech validation team so we can proceed with the AWS listing checks: 
1) Runtime image verification — please provide the digest (sha256) for the Linux container images you plan to publish to the AWS Marketplace (both inference runtime and sidecar metrics exporter).
2) Network ingress — confirm which public endpoints (hostnames/IP ranges) your hosted control plane will call back to for metering and telemetry, and provide required port ranges. The marketplace team needs explicit firewall allowlist entries.
3) Billing contract flow — provide the HubSpot or procurement ID you will use for marketplace reconciliations (we need to map to our Marketplace Partner ID).

If you prefer, we can accept the artifacts in a secured S3 bucket or via your partner Drive link. Targeting validation complete by Tue 3/30.
